questions.question: Parsec is a unit of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**length.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The parsec is defined as a unit of length or distance** which is used to measure the large distances to astronomical objects outside the solar system.

 
 
• One parsec is defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond.
 
• A parsec is equivalent to 3.26 light-years.
 
• A parsec is a distance from the Sun to an astronomical object which has a parallax angle of one arcsecond.

questions.question: In 1977, who became the President of the Janata Party, which formed a coalition government at the centre with Morarji Desai as the Prime Minister?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandra Shekhar.**__

__
 
• Chandra Shekhar Singh

 
 
• He became the President of the Janata Party in 1977.
 
• He was an Indian politician who served as the **8th Prime Minister of India, between 10 November 1990 and 21 June 1991.**
 
• He headed a minority government of a breakaway faction of the Janata Dal with outside support from the Indian National Congress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Janata Party:

 
 
• The Janata Party was a political party that was founded as an amalgam of Indian political parties opposed to the Emergency that was imposed between 1975 to 1977 by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi of the Indian National Congress.
 
• In the 1977 general election, the party defeated the Congress and Janata leader Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress prime minister in independent modern India's history.
 
• Nitish Kumar started his political career with Janata Party.
 
• The rationale of the formation was that of preserving national security.
 
• When the State of Emergency was lifted and new elections called in 1977, opposition political parties such as the Congress (O), Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Bharatiya Lok Dal as well as defectors from the Congress (R) joined to form the Janata Party, which won a sweeping majority in the Indian Parliament.

questions.question: In connection with the issue of adoption of villages by parliamentarians, a scheme named ‘SAGY’ was launched. What does the 'A' in SAGY stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adarsh.**__

__
 
• SAGY stands for **Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana**

 
 
• Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana launched on **11th October 2014**, on the birth anniversary of **Jai Prakash Narayan.**
 
• The goal of Sansad Adarsha Gram Yojana was to develop three Adarsh Villages (Model Village) by 2019, of which one was to be achieved by 2016. Thereafter, five such Adarsh Grams (one per year) will be selected and developed by 2024.
 
• Members of Parliament (MPs) are responsible for developing the socio-economic and physical infrastructure in Adarsh Gram.
 
• Gram Panchayat is the basic unit for development.
 
• Gram Panchayats with a** population of 3000-5000 in plain areas and 1000-3000 in hilly**, tribal and difficult areas are to be selected by Members of Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following is an award for contribution in the field of science and technology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar (SSB) Award.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The "Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar (SSB) Prize for Science and Technology" is a science award in India.

 
 
• It was awarded annually for outstanding contributions to science and technology.
 
• It is one of the highest multidisciplinary science awards in India.
 
• It is given by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The award is named after Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar.

 
 
• Shanti Swaroop Bhatnagar is popularly known as the "father of Research Laboratories in India".
 
• He was the founding director-general of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
 
 
 
• It was first awarded in 1958.
 
• Kariamanickam Srinivasa Krishnan was the first recipient of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize.
 
• Fourteen scientists were announced winners of the prestigious Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in 2020.

questions.question: Which of the following is the SI unit for measuring the amount of a substance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mole (mol).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The amount of substance in a given sample of matter is the 'number of discrete atomic-scale particles in it' divided by the 'Avogadro constant NA.
 
• Mole__ is an **SI unit used for measuring the amount of a substance.**
 
• The amount of substance is the number of particles that constitute the substance.
 
• One mole (mol) contains exactly 6.02214076 × 1023 elementary entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: The rules made for the ______ were written down in a book called ‘Vinaya Pitaka'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhist sangha.**__

__
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka** is a book related to the rules of the Buddhist Sangha.
 
• The Vinaya was preserved by being memorized and chanted by generations of monks and nuns.
 
• The Vinaya-Pitaka, or "basket of discipline," is the first of three parts of the Tipitaka, a collection of the earliest Buddhist texts.
 
• The Vinaya records the Buddha's rules of discipline for monks and nuns. 
 
• It also contains stories about the first Buddhist monks and nuns and how they lived.
 
• The Vinaya was not written down during the Buddha's lifetime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vaishnavism: 

 
 
• ​In South India, Vaishnava saints are known as Alvars.
 
• They preached complete devotion towards God Vishnu.
 
• Their religious songs were collectively called Prabandhas.
 
• It laid emphasis on the doctrine of Avataras (incarnations).
 
 
 
• **The Lingayats**
 
 
• ​Basaveshwara or Basavanna was an Indian 12th-century statesman, philosopher, poet and Lingayat saint and a social reformer in Karnataka.
 
• He founded the Lingayats follower of shiva.

questions.question: Atoms of which element combines with hydrogen to give water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen.**__

__
 
• **2 grams of hydrogen and 16 grams of oxygen** form a molecule of water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd4b4c1c1232e3e5a2839b344f73cee8c5b6e402a96db412562813676306ffe2.png] ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Water (H2O) is classified as a polar molecule because of its polar covalent bond and bent shape.
 
• The bent shape means most of the negative charge from the oxygen atom is on one side of the molecule and the positive charge of the hydrogen atoms is on the other side of the molecule.

questions.question: ______ festival in the Bastar region is celebrated along with the worship of the local goddess, Kesharpal Kesharpalin Devi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Madai.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Charama and Kurna** communities of **the Kanker district, tribes of Bastar, celebrate the Madai Festival in the state of Chhattisgarh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phool Dei - **It is known as **the harvest festival of the state of Uttarakhand**, Phool Dei is an auspicious folk festival that **welcomes the spring season** in the state.
 
• **Khatarua -** It is the **special festival of pastoral- agricultural Kumaon society in Uttarakhand** and is observed annually on the first day of Ashvin, the seventh month of the lunisolar Hindu calendar.
 
 
• The festival** honours farm animals and is believed to protect rural livestock from all evil**.
 
 
 
• **Harela - **Harela means **a** **day of green** and is celebrated in the month of Shravan to worship Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. People across Uttarakhand, especially** the Kumaun region, associate greenery with prosperity**.

questions.question: The Kamaicha is a bowed lute played by the Manganiars of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__West Rajasthan.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Kamaicha**:

 
 
• It is a **bowed lute **played by **the Manganiars of west Rajasthan**. 
 
• The whole instrument is** one piece of wood**, **the spherical bowl** extending into a neck and fingerboard; the resonator is covered with leather and the upper portion with wood.
 
• There are **four main strings **and a number of subsidiary ones passing over a thin bridge.
 
• It links the **sub-continent to Western Asia and Africa** and is considered by some scholars to be the oldest instrument, with the exception of the **Ravana Hatta or Ravana Hasta Veena.**

questions.question: Weber per second is equivalent to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Volt.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weber per second** is equivalent to **Volt.**
 
• The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).

 
• Magnetic flux is a measurement of the total magnetic field which passes through a given area.
 
• Magnetic flux is the product of the average magnetic field times the perpendicular area that it penetrates.
 
• The SI unit of the magnetic field (B) is weber/meter2 (Wbm-2) or tesla.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** 

 
• **Ampere - **It is the unit of **Electric Current**.
 
• **Volt - **It is the derived unit of **electric potential**.
 
• **Ohm - **It is the unit of** electrical resistance**.
 
• **Coulomb - **It is the SI unit of **electric charge.**

questions.question: Alamgir was the title of which Mughal emperor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb.**__

__
 
• Alamgir was the title of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• He was the son of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal and was born in Dahod on 3rd November 1618.
 
• He executed the ninth Sikh guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur in 1675.
 
• The territorial climax of the Mughal empire was reached during Aurangzeb.
 
• Aurangzeb discovered cases of misappropriation of funds sent to Arabia, he favoured their distribution in India which, he thought, **“was as much a house of God as Mecca”.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Babur (1526-1530 AD):

 
 
• He was the founder of the Mughal dynasty in India.
 
 
 
• Humayun (1530-1540 AD):
 
 
• He was a son of Babur.
 
• Not much control over the kingdom.
 
• Shershah Suri was his biggest obstacle.
 
 
 
• Akbar (1556-1605 AD):
 
 
• He was a son of Humayun.
 
• He established the throne well in Delhi.
 
• He was one of the modest rulers of the Mughal empire.
 
 
 
• Jahangir (1605-1627 AD):
 
 
• He was a son of Akbar.
 
• His name was Salim.
 
• Jahangir was his title.
 
 
 
• Shahjahan (1627-1658 AD):
 
 
• He was a successor of Jahangir.
 
• He expanded the empire towards Deccan, N-W Frontier, and East India.

questions.question: World Leprosy Day 2021 was celebrated in India on ______ January 2021.

• **30 January **is selected as a remembrance of the death anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

• World Leprosy Day is celebrated on the last Sunday of January every year all over the world to increase knowledge about it and propagate the need and importance of eradicating the disease.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 

 
• **Leprosy** is also known as Hansen’s disease.
 
• It is an infectious disease that is caused by a **bacillus Mycobacterium leprae**.
 
• The disease has been named after Gerhard Henrik Armauer Hansen who was a Norwegian physician.
 
• Hansen proved that leprosy is not a hereditary disease but is caused by a bacterium.
 
• The disease is a curable disease and treatment at the early stage can prevent any disability.
 
• It can cause progressive and permanent damage to the skin, nerves, limbs, and eyes if it is left untreated.
 
• The incubation period of the disease is 5 years usually. Symptoms of the disease can be seen within 1 year but it could also take 20 years or even more years to occur.
